questions.primary_text: Participation to a Study of the impact of AI and explainable AI to Human Performance at a Pattern Identification Task
questions.secondary_text:
Scientific Supervisor

Prof. Sébastien Harispe

Project Objectives

The aim of this project is to study the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and explainable AI on human performance in carrying out a task of pattern identification in images.

What Is Expected of You

You will need to detect the presence of patterns in images containing geometric symbols. For each image presented to you, will have to answer a question within a limited time. The pattern to detect will be communicated to you in the form of a question (for example: ”In the image, is there exactly four squares?”).

You are expected to perform as well as possible. Your performance will be evaluated based on the number of correct answers during the main experimental phase. You will have to answer the questions within the allocated time for each image. Responding faster will not improve your score. However, if you fail to respond within the allocated time, it will be counted as an error.

The protocol will start with an introductive phase, in which you will have the opportunity to train for the tasks. Your performance will only start to be recorded during the main experimental phase.

You will also be expected to answer several surveys during the protocol.

Depending on your random assignment into a group, you might receive the assistance of an AI to perform the tasks.

Your Right to Withdraw from the Study

You have the right to withdraw from the study at any time.

Your Right to Ask Questions

Since the study is conducted online, it will not be possible to ask questions during the participation. However you can send questions before or after the experiment to jules.leguy@mines-ales.fr.

Confidentiality and Privacy

The information collected in this form is recorded in a file by Jules Leguy for research purposes, specifically to study human performance in a pattern recognition task. The legal basis for this data processing is your consent.

The collected data will only be shared with the following recipients:

  • Jules Leguy
  • Andon Tchechmedjiev

The data will be kept for five years after the scientific publication (expected in 2026).

You may request access to your personal data, request corrections, or exercise your right to restrict the processing of your data. For more information on your rights, consult the CNIL website.

The right to data deletion is excluded during the retention period, as deletion would compromise the research.

To exercise these rights or ask questions regarding data processing within this framework, you may contact: andon.tchechmedjiev@mines-ales.fr.

If, after contacting us, you believe that your “Informatics and Liberties” rights have not been respected, you may submit a complaint to the CNIL (French Data Protection Authority).

Expected Benefits of the Study

You will receive financial compensation at an hourly rate of €8.00. You will also receive a bonus of €0.05 for each correct answer during the main experimental phase.

Possible Risks

The risks involved in these tests are no different from those encountered when performing a standard computer task.

Right to Withdraw Consent

I understand that my participation in this research is voluntary and that I may refuse to participate. If I so choose, I am FREE TO STOP PARTICIPATING AT ANY TIME, without having to provide justification. I will inform the Scientific Supervisor in writing at the following address: jules.leguy@mines-ales.fr.

I understand that my decision to participate in this research does not release either the researchers or the host institution from their professional and legal obligations toward me. I acknowledge my right to access and correct personal information concerning me. I understand that no personally identifiable information will be processed electronically.

Acknowledgment of Prior Information

The scientific supervisor has informed me of the nature and objectives of this research, as well as its procedures, potential benefits, and possible risks.

Acceptance of Conditions

I agree to comply with the constraints explained and specified in the information document, both to minimize risks and to ensure the proper completion of the protocol.

I agree to comply with the confidentiality rules applicable to this research, as explained to me beforehand.

Other Information

As part of this research, all DATA AND INFORMATION concerning me will remain STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL. I authorize their consultation only by persons designated by the researcher and, where applicable, by representatives of the authorities.

I am informed that certain personal data, once anonymized, may be subject to computerized processing to make them Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR), in line with the principles of open science promoted by the European Commission.

Consent

title: Introduction
body_text:
Thank you for participating to this experiment.

You will have to perform a series of tasks which will consist in identyfing patterns in images. Your goal is to maximize your performance, by trying to provide the right answer for every image. Your bonus financial reward will depend on your overall performance during the main experimental phase.

Please read the information above carefully, as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below. You can take notes if you wish to.
button_text: I read and understood the instructions

title: Let's jump in
body_text:
Before giving you further instructions, you will perform a first training task in order to discover the interface. This task will not count towards your score and remuneration, and the results will not be recorded. You will be presented with a series of 5 images of symbols of colors, and you will have to answer a question regarding the image. For this task and few other tasks of the Introduction, you will be informed if the decision was right or wrong after each decision.

As for every task later, the question will be the same for every image of the task. The question will usually change every new task, except for few tasks of the Introduction.

Please read the information above carefully, as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below. You can take notes if you wish to.

title: Protocol structure
body_text:
The protocol will last about 30 minutes and is organized as follows.


To continue your familiarization with the task and the interface, you will enter the acclimation phase, which consists of two tasks of 5 images each.

Then, you will start the preparation phase for the main experiment, which will consist of 4 tasks of 10 questions each. The tasks will be very similar to the tasks of the main experiment. This phase will conclude the introduction

Then, the main experiment will start. It will be divided into 2 main sessions. Each session consists in solving 4 tasks of 10 questions each, that will count towards your score and bonus remuneration. Every 2 tasks, you will have to answer a small survey about the tasks you just performed.

Finally, you will enter the closing phase, in which you will have to answer a final survey to terminate the protocol.

Please note that your actions and answers will only be recorded during the Main experimental phase and the Closing phase, and that the tasks that count towards your performance and bonus remuneration are all part of the Main experimental phase.

Please read the information above carefully, as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below. You can take notes if you wish to.

title: Main experiment
body_text:
The introduction is over. You are now entering the main experimental phase, in which your answers as well as your performance at the tasks will be recorded. Your performance during this phase will count towards your bonus remuneration. As a reminder, the structure of the experiment is described in the diagram below.


This phase is divided in 2 sessions. In each session, you must perform 2 tasks, answer a first survey about those tasks, then you must perform another 2 tasks and answer a second survey about those 2 latter tasks. There is no right or wrong answers to the surveys; only your score during the tasks will count towards your bonus remuneration.

Note that you will not be given your score anymore at the end of each task. Your score on all tasks of the main experimental phase will be given to you at the end of the protocol.

Please read the information above carefully as you will not be able to return to this page once you click the button below. You can take notes if you wish to.
